summary: Hugo Valvanne (1894–1961) was an Indologist. He earned an M.A. from the University of Helsinki, where he studied under J. N. Reuter around 1913–1917.

Hugo Winckler (1863–1913) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1883 to 1887 and later held a post there from circa 1891 to 1913.
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University, where Yi-hsun Huang served as MA supervisor (attested in 2011).
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who held a post at the University of Hong Kong and studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested in 2007).

Huimin (b. 1954), a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He served at Taipei National University of the Arts (~1992–2017), the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–2007), and as President of Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (~2014–2022).
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University. Lin's MA supervisor was Kuo-wei Liu, and additional teachers included Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under supervisor Kirill Solonin and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang (b. 1951) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Zhang studied at the University of Tokyo and held a lecturer post at Dongguk University (attested 1996).

Humberto Maturana (1928–2021) was a philosopher. He studied at the University of Chile, UCL, and Harvard (doctorate, 1956–1958). He held positions at MIT, the University of Chile, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and co-founded Instituto Matríztica in 2000.

Humphrey William Codrington (1879–1942) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Winchester College (~1892–1898) and New College (B.A., ~1898–1902) before serving in the Ceylon Civil Service from 1903 to 1932.

Hung Wu (b. 1945), a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology, studied at CAFA and Harvard (PhD ~1980–1987). He held professorships at Harvard, the University of Chicago (since 1994), NYU (2011–2012), and Oxford (2015–2016), and curated at the Smart Museum.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under the supervision of Mark Allon (attested 2013).

Huston Smith (1919–2016) was a scholar of religion and philosophy who studied at Central Methodist University, University of Chicago (PhD), and under Zuigan Goto. He taught at Denver, Washington University, MIT (1958–1973), Syracuse (1973–1983), and UC Berkeley (~1984–1999).

Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2010), advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, studying under Kapila Abhayawansa.
Hwansoo Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held posts as a professor at Duke University (attested 2017) and as Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

Hyacinth Bitchurin (1777–1853) was a scholar of sinology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After studying at Kazan Theological Academy, he held posts there, at Tobolsk Theological Seminary, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Hyakudai Sakamoto (1928–2020) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1951). He held posts at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1964–1999), Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences (~1999–2003), and The Open University of Japan.

Hyejeong Choi works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Choi earned a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and was a Visiting Researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture (attested 2015).

Hyla Stuntz Converse (1920–1990) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned a B.D. from Union Theological Seminary (~1946–1949), a Ph.D. from Columbia University (~1965–1971), and held a post at Oklahoma State University in 1974.
